packages.title: ECUK 2024 final energy 128.1 mtoe QA
facts: DESNZ reports UK final energy consumption excluding non-energy use at 128.1 mtoe in 2024.
Final energy is energy used by people and businesses in day-to-day activities.
The measure is sourced from UK energy balances.
Energy consumption is not a GHG emissions amount.
No parcel energy use is inferred.

packages.title: ECUK final energy 2.6 percent rise QA
facts: ECUK reports 2024 final energy consumption was 2.6% higher than in 2023.
The comparison excludes non-energy use.
The percentage refers to energy consumption rather than emissions.
Annual national movement does not imply equal changes by sector or property.
No parcel trend is inferred.

packages.title: ECUK final energy 7.9 percent below 2019 QA
facts: ECUK reports 2024 final energy consumption was 7.9% lower than pre-pandemic 2019 levels.
The comparison uses the same final-energy concept.
Historical comparison requires consistent energy-balance definitions.
Energy level differences are not automatically proportional to GHG differences.
No parcel baseline is inferred.

packages.title: ECUK final versus primary energy definition QA
facts: ECUK distinguishes final energy consumption from primary energy consumption.
Final energy describes energy used by consumers and businesses.
Primary energy relates to total fuel inputs, including fuels used to generate electricity.
The two measures have different denominators and system boundaries.
They must not be substituted in parcel emissions calculations.

packages.title: ECUK SIC reference-table methodology break QA
facts: ECUK 2025 introduced an updated reference table for allocating industrial consumption to 2-digit SIC divisions.
The newer reference table is used for 2021 onwards while the earlier table is used for 2020 and earlier.
The change improves allocation of bioenergy and waste and sector consistency.
Method changes can create interpretation breaks in detailed industry series.
No parcel inference is made from SIC allocation.

packages.title: ECUK services energy 3.8 percent rise QA
facts: ECUK reports services-sector energy consumption increased by 3.8% between 2023 and 2024.
The absolute increase is reported at about 0.8 mtoe.
DESNZ links the change partly to higher natural-gas and petroleum consumption in services subsectors.
Services energy consumption is not direct services-sector GHG measurement.
No building parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: Energy Trends renewable capacity versus generation QA
facts: Energy Trends publishes renewable electricity capacity and generation as separate measures.
Installed capacity is a power rating while generation is energy produced over time.
Capacity cannot be treated as observed generation.
Neither metric alone is a GHG emissions measurement.
No parcel generation or emissions value is inferred.

packages.title: Heat Networks Planning Database project-stage QA
facts: The Heat Networks Planning Database tracks district and communal heat-network projects.
Project stages include inception, planning, construction, operation and decommissioning.
A project's presence or stage does not measure heat delivered or GHG emissions.
Planning-database evidence is project-development evidence.
No parcel emissions value is inferred from project status.

packages.title: Heat Networks Planning Database quarterly update-lag QA
facts: DESNZ states the Heat Networks Planning Database is updated during the month following the end of each quarter.
The current dataset therefore has a reporting lag relative to real-world project changes.
Planning applications and developer contact are source inputs.
A database timestamp is not an operational-meter timestamp.
No real-time parcel value is inferred.

packages.title: UK ETS 2026 additional 983,000 allowances QA
facts: UK ETS guidance states the revised 2026 auction calendar increased auction volume by 983,000 allowances for maritime inclusion.
The revision was reflected in the 1 July 2026 auction calendar.
Allowance volume is a market-supply quantity rather than verified emissions.
The additional volume is spread across remaining 2026 auctions starting in August.
No parcel emissions value is inferred from allowance supply.

packages.title: UK ETS 2026 nearly 53 million allowances across 25 auctions QA
facts: UK ETS guidance states just under 53 million allowances are scheduled across 25 auctions in 2026 after revision.
Auctions began in January 2026 and continue fortnightly.
Auctioned allowances are tradable compliance units.
Auction quantity is not the same as annual verified emissions.
No facility or parcel emissions value is inferred from auction supply.

packages.title: UK ETS maritime market-calendar revision QA
facts: The 2026 auction calendar was revised to reflect inclusion of maritime emissions in the UK ETS from July 2026.
Maritime scope affects allowance-market supply planning.
Scheme inclusion does not itself report a vessel's verified emissions.
Compliance evidence must remain separate from allowance-market configuration.
No port or parcel emissions value is inferred.

packages.title: UK ETS secondary-market activity versus emissions QA
facts: UK ETS participants can trade allowances on a secondary market.
Secondary-market transactions are ownership transfers of allowances.
Trading volume or price is not equivalent to verified emissions.
Verified emissions and surrender obligations require separate compliance evidence.
No parcel value is inferred from market trades.

packages.title: England July drought 3 percent LTA rainfall QA
facts: The Environment Agency reported only 3% of long-term-average rainfall for the referenced July period in its 10 to 16 July 2026 drought summary.
The statistic describes hydrological conditions rather than emissions.
Dry-weather conditions can affect water demand and abstraction restrictions.
Rainfall percentage is not a GHG indicator.
No parcel emissions value is inferred.

packages.title: England reservoir storage 78.8 percent drought QA
facts: The Environment Agency reported England reservoir storage at 78.8% in the 10 to 16 July 2026 summary.
This was around 5 percentage points below the long-term average for the time of year.
Reservoir storage is a water-resource state variable.
Water-resource status is not direct evidence of GHG emissions.
No property emissions value is inferred.

packages.title: Heatwave water demand around 20 percent above normal QA
facts: The Environment Agency reported water companies experiencing around a 20% increase in demand above normal during the heatwave referenced in the July 2026 drought summary.
The figure is an operational water-demand indicator.
Higher water demand does not directly quantify energy use or GHG emissions.
The statistic is time- and event-specific.
No parcel emissions value is inferred.

packages.title: Water abstraction 20 cubic metres per day threshold QA
facts: Environment Agency guidance states abstractions of 20 cubic metres per day or less can be exempt subject to stated conditions.
Abstraction above 20 cubic metres per day is likely to require a licence.
A licence threshold is a regulatory quantity rather than an emissions metric.
Water abstraction can be consumptive or non-consumptive depending on the activity.
No GHG or parcel value is inferred from the licensing threshold.

packages.title: Cross-source parcel inference guard 106 QA
facts: Batch 106 sources operate at national, residence, territorial, industry, local-authority, market, project or hydrological scales.
None of the reviewed sources establishes cadastral geometry for gas_emissions_3 parcels.
Activity, capacity, allowance, intensity, project-stage and water indicators are not silently converted to CO2e.
Provisional and final statuses are preserved separately.
Parcel binding remains false until an explicit verified parcel-level source and geometry join exists.
